item.title: Agentic AI and Entrepreneurship: Bright and Dark Sides Across the Venture Cycle
item.content:encoded:
Victor Tiberius, University of Potsdam

Alhamzah Al Sayed Noor, |

Mumtaz Ali Memon, |

This special issue examines how agentic AI systems—capable of perceiving context, planning, using tools, and learning with limited supervision—transform entrepreneurship across all venture development stages. Unlike passive technologies, agentic AI acts as an active co-agent in entrepreneurial decision-making.

The call recognizes both opportunities and risks. Agentic AI can enhance opportunity recognition, market analysis, and strategic decisions while reducing information gaps. However, it poses risks including overdependence, algorithmic bias, accountability gaps, and threats to entrepreneurial autonomy and identity.

The special issue welcomes empirical and theoretical studies from emerging and advanced economies exploring when agentic AI enables value creation versus creating risks. It encourages theoretical connections with entrepreneurship theories and methodologically diverse research including experiments, qualitative studies, and computational methods.

Appel publié par Journal of Entrepreneurship in Emerging Economies. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Agentic AI and opportunity recognition
  • Entrepreneurial decision-making under uncertainty
  • Human-AI co-agency and entrepreneurial judgment
  • New venture creation with agentic AI
  • AI-native startups and autonomous venture development
  • Business model innovation
  • Venture scaling, growth, and internationalisation
  • Entrepreneurial exit decisions
  • Agentic AI benefits: speed, efficiency, creativity, resource mobilisation
  • Agentic AI risks: bias, dependency, autonomy loss, accountability
  • Entrepreneurial cognition, identity, and creativity
  • Trust, resistance, and adoption of agentic AI
  • Entrepreneurial ecosystems
  • Emerging economies and resource-constrained contexts
  • Comparative studies across emerging and advanced economies
  • Sustainable and inclusive entrepreneurship
  • Governance and responsible use of agentic AI
  • Methodological approaches for studying agentic AI and entrepreneurship

Timeline

  • September 1, 2026: Opening date for manuscript submissions
  • December 1, 2026: Closing date for manuscript submissions

item.title: Ethics and Entrepreneurship: Foundations and Philosophical Perspectives
item.content:encoded:
Tina Dacin, Wilfrid Laurier University

Robin Holt, University of Bristol

Jean Clarke, Emlyon Business School

Jaco Lok, Macquarie University

Max Ganzin, Macquarie University

This special issue examines the ethical foundations of entrepreneurship, positioning ethics as central to entrepreneurial practice rather than a constraint on it. The issue brings together entrepreneurship studies and philosophical ethics to explore how venture creation, opportunity recognition, and stakeholder engagement involve fundamental questions about responsibility, justice, and human flourishing. It investigates the tension between entrepreneurship's capacity for creativity and disruption and concerns about commodification and self-optimization.

The special issue welcomes diverse methodological and disciplinary perspectives examining how philosophical traditions such as virtue ethics, phenomenology, pragmatism, and deontology illuminate entrepreneurial practice. It particularly emphasizes entrepreneurial decision-making under uncertainty and fluidity, where ethical judgment must balance competing stakeholder interests without reliance on established protocols. The issue seeks papers exploring how entrepreneurship and ethics can deepen each other's understanding through examining contingency, creativity, authenticity, care, and emerging futures.

Appel publié par Journal of Business Ethics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Philosophical dimensions of ethics and how different philosophical traditions inform understanding of entrepreneurship as an ethical practice
  • Phenomenology of the entrepreneurial experience, uncertainty, autonomy, and decision-making
  • The entrepreneur and ethical subjectivity, agency, embodiment, and identity
  • Ethics and rule-breaking in entrepreneurial contexts
  • Stakeholder relations, trust-building, and ethical objectives
  • Whether entrepreneurship is inherently ethical or exploitative
  • Entrepreneurship and technological mediation in the digital age
  • Ethics, value, and the framing of entrepreneurial goals and opportunities
  • Temporal dimensions of entrepreneurial ethics and long-term considerations

Timeline

  • September 30, 2026: Submission deadline
